metadata.title: Why Partial JSON Can Be a Valid Object Before the Closing Brace Arrives
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: why does a jsonSnapshot mid-stream already parse as a valid object with no closing brace yet? Lands the carry-out that a valid snapshot means the shape is safe to read, not that the values inside are finished.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B04 (four-chunk {"q": "solar case, paid off by splitting each snapshot into shape-safe vs. value-still-growing)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a half-finished JSON string must be broken until the brace arrives. It isn't — the SDK hands back a usable object after every chunk. So how does a partial string already parse as one?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'This half-finished string must be broken, right?', hesitates on 'broken', corrects to 'usable', lands the real question

props.text:

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('broken' -> 'usable') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: When Claude streams a tool call, JSON.parse demands a complete document — feed it a half-finished string and it throws. So the natural guess is that a streaming snapshot behaves the same way: broken, or empty, until the brace lands. Read it early, and you'd expect an error, not an object.

shot.new_visual_element: A half-finished string splitting into a THROWS path (standard parser) and a question-marked path (streaming snapshot)

production_viz.label: Two paths, one unresolved
production_viz.mechanic: A card labelled 'HALF-FINISHED STRING' on cream, feeding two arrows. Top arrow to a card labelled 'JSON.parse' which throws (crossed with terracotta X, captioned 'THROWS'). Bottom arrow to a card labelled '.on(inputJson)' with a large question mark, captioned 'streaming snapshot — ?'.

beats.narration_text: Here's the concrete case. A search tool streams the argument `{"q": "solar` across four chunks. `.on('inputJson')` fires with `jsonSnapshot` equal to `{}`, then `{"q":""}`, then `{"q":"sol"}`, then `{"q":"solar"}` — four snapshots, and every single one already a complete, parseable object.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - four snapshots ticking across a timeline, each stamped VALID

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - four snapshots, each already valid
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A horizontal timeline with four tick marks. At each tick, a small card appears in sequence: '{}', then '{"q":""}', then '{"q":"sol"}', then '{"q":"solar"}' (monospace, terracotta border). Each card gets a terracotta VALID stamp the instant it appears. Header reads 'search_database streams {"q": "solar'. THIS FOUR-CARD TIMELINE COMPOSITION RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: Here's why. The parser keeps a stack of every object and array it has opened. The instant a chunk ends, it closes each open structure with a zero-value default — an empty string, an empty object — and hands back whatever that produces. Nothing waits for the real closing brace; the parser supplies its own.

shot.new_visual_element: A token stream feeding a stack; the stack sealing shut into a complete tree at each cut point

production_viz.label: The stack seals itself shut
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a token stream ('{', '"q"', ':', '"sol') feeding into a vertical stack of open-structure markers ('{ open', 'string open'). Right: at a cut point (dashed terracotta line), the stack markers each sprout a closing counterpart ('}' , '"') labelled 'zero-value default', producing a complete tree diagram, captioned 'no real closing brace here'.

beats.narration_text: So back to the search call: `{}` isn't an empty query — it's a query string that hasn't started arriving yet. And `{"q":"sol"}` isn't the final query either — three more characters are still on the wire. A valid snapshot tells you the shape is safe to read; it doesn't tell you the value inside has stopped changing.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the same four snapshots, now each split into shape: safe and value: still growing

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - shape-safe vs. value-still-growing
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 TIMELINE COMPOSITION RETURNS: the same four snapshot cards ('{}', '{"q":""}', '{"q":"sol"}', '{"q":"solar"}') now each split by a horizontal divider into two labels: top 'SHAPE: SAFE' (ink), bottom 'VALUE: STILL GROWING' (terracotta) — except the final card, whose bottom label reads 'VALUE: DONE' in ink (no accent — it is not the thing still changing).

beats.narration_text: The parser closes every open structure for you — so a valid snapshot tells you the shape is safe to read, not that the values inside it are finished.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I'm streaming a tool call with the Anthropic TypeScript SDK and I see partial JSON arriving via the inputJson event. Walk me through why each chunk's jsonSnapshot is already a valid JS object before the closing brace arrives, and show me how to read a field from it safely mid-stream without waiting for the tool_use_delta done event.
